title: MaplePay pilot capacity governance and surge runbook check-in
summary: Weekly POC sync to review last week's stress runs, validate autoscale thresholds for Dedicated capacity, agree on surge runbook changes and next stress test. Security asks re: KMS and audit logs; action items to update runbook, run a KV-cache-heavy test, and share revised sizing spreadsheet.
action_items: Priya Nair (Redwood SE) - Update surge runbook with explicit fallback to smaller quantized model and push to shared Google Drive by 2027-11-05
Marcus Liu (MaplePay) - Run 20m KV-cache-heavy stress test (70% cache hit target) and upload results by 2027-11-08
Jordan Blake (AE) - Send revised Dedicated sizing spreadsheet with cost delta scenarios (reserve buffer at 10/20/30%) by 2027-11-04
Lina Ortiz (MaplePay Security) - Share KMS key rotation cadence and confirm acceptable audit retention window by 2027-11-09
next_steps: Schedule coordinated load run (Nov 10 tentative) with Redwood SE on call
Agree on final autoscale cooldown (suggested 45s) and burst eviction policy
Redwood to provide runbook PR and playbook link
Customer to validate SSO access for Redwood runbook during test
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-02 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Evelyn Park (MaplePay Head of Platform), Marcus Liu (MaplePay Infra), Lina Ortiz (MaplePay Security), Samir Patel (PM)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we have a full house. quick agenda — recap last week's stress runs, talk autoscale thresholds, reserve / burst behavior, security asks, and then next run scheduling. sound good?
[00:12] Evelyn: Yep that's right, excited to go over the numbers.
[00:18] Marcus: Sorry team, just background noise, I'm on headphones now.
[00:22] Priya: No worries. I'll pull up the test summary. so high level — the 2-hour ramp with synthetic traffic hit our target throughput and we saw the Dedicated pool scale from 2 to 6 GPUs under the current autoscale policy.
[00:36] Marcus: Right, the scaling worked but we noticed sustained latency spikes when the KV cache miss rate went above about 35%. Took latency from 85ms p50 to over 300ms p95.
[00:50] Jordan: Ok that's interesting. was that during the initial warmup or after the burst?
[00:53] Marcus: It was during the steady-state after the burst — likely because the model had to fetch more context without effective prefix cache, and the batch sizes also grew.
[01:05] Priya: Mm-hmm, that's consistent with what we saw. the runtime delayed some of the larger batches to prioritize latency SLOs, which increased p95 for a short window. we have a knob to cap batching growth or force earlier KV warming.
[01:20] Evelyn: We need to avoid those 300ms spikes — users will notice. what's the recommended approach? reduce batch sizes or increase reserve buffer?
[01:28] Priya: Two levers: reserve buffer (so you have pre-provisioned capacity for bursts) and batch cap (limit how many tokens/batches can accumulate). for your workload we think a modest reserve buffer of 15-20% plus an autoscale cooldown around 45 seconds gives a good balance.
[01:45] Samir: Quick question — how does fallback to a smaller quantized model affect quality? we have acceptance criteria about hallucination rate.
[01:53] Priya: Good call. fallback to a lower-precision variant will drop mean token quality slightly — maybe a small increase in error on synth tests — but it's usually acceptable for short bursts if you prefer availability over 100% fidelity. we can gate it behind a canary or threshold so it's only used when latency breaches a hard SLO.
[02:12] Marcus: Another practical note: when eviction happens from the reserve buffer it's not instant; we saw a 10-15s window where requests queued. can that be reduced?
[02:21] Jordan: The queueing is partly from burst ramp and partly API client retry patterns. we can change client backoff or enable immediate scale-up policies. also adding a soft-priority lane for authenticated low-latency requests might help.
[02:35] Lina: On the security side, we need to confirm key management. our KMS policy requires per-tenant keys and 90-day rotation window. is Redwood compatible? and what about audit logs?
[02:47] Priya: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS in VPC deployments; for Dedicated hosted we'll wire KMS integrations. audit logs — we can stream request and model meta logs to your SIEM for 180 days. we'll send the SOC2 / audit doc.
[03:03] Lina: Great, please share specifics of the log schema. also need to confirm that the model KV cache doesn't persist PII — currently our test set had some synthetic PII we scrubbed, but want to be safe.
[03:16] Priya: KV caches are ephemeral in-memory and not written to long-term storage by default. if you enable explicit cache snapshots that's an opt-in feature and we'd need to coordinate retention. we'll add a note in the runbook.
[03:30] Evelyn: Back to the reserve size — can you quantify cost delta if we choose 10% vs 30% reserve?
[03:37] Jordan: Yes, Priya has a sizing spreadsheet. Priya, can you summarize the hit?
[03:41] Priya: Sure. at current throughput, 10% reserve is roughly a 6% increase in steady-state monthly cost; 30% reserve is ~18% increase. but 30% gives headroom for big traffic swings — also reduces fallback frequency. I'll send the sheet with scenarios.
[03:58] Marcus: For the next stress run we want to simulate KV miss heavy traffic — to validate the early-warning thresholds. can Redwood orchestrate that?
[04:07] Priya: Yes, we can coordinate, we can also run the test jointly so we can tweak the cooldowns in real-time. recommended target: 20 minute sustained burst at 2.5x baseline with cache miss ramping to 70%.
[04:21] Samir: We'll need runbook steps so our on-call can trigger the test and rollback if things degrade.
[04:26] Jordan: We'll provide a playbook with explicit rollback — steps include aborting the test, forcing fallback to hosted smaller model, and temporarily increasing batch cap.
[04:36] Evelyn: What about SSO access for our infra team during the test window? we don't want to open long-lived accounts.
[04:42] Jordan: We can create ephemeral SSO sessions scoped to the test window. we'll document the exact role mappings and ask you to validate.
[04:50] Lina: Also can you confirm what telemetry you'll need from our side? e.g., client-side latency, request traces, sample prompts?
[04:57] Priya: We'll want client-side request traces and a small sample of prompts (redacted of course). we'll provide a template for the metrics we ingest (qps, p50/p95/p99, cache hit, batch size distribution).
[05:10] Marcus: During the test last week we saw autoscale flapping when cooldown was 20s — it scaled up and down repeatedly. would increasing cooldown to 45s prevent flapping?
[05:19] Priya: Yes, increasing cooldown reduces churn. 45s is a good starting point; plus adding a minimum up-time for scaled instances (e.g., 120s) helps amortize spin costs.
[05:30] Samir: If we set high min-up and cooldown, what's the risk for over-provisioning cost? we don't want to pay for idle GPUs.
[05:37] Priya: Tradeoff is cost vs stability. that's why reserve buffer is useful — reserve plus slightly longer cooldown reduces the number of spin-ups while keeping latency bounded. that's in the spreadsheet scenarios.
[05:48] Jordan: Quick pivot — on fallback model route: we recommend a staged fallback: 1) progressive quantized variant on same family, 2) smaller architecture if still degraded, 3) read-only cached responses for non-critical routes. that sequence reduces quality loss.
[06:05] Evelyn: Can we define thresholds? like p95 > 400ms for 30s triggers fallback 1, then p95 > 600ms for 60s triggers fallback 2?
[06:14] Priya: Absolutely, we can encode that into the runbook and the platform has alerting hooks to flip a fallback flag.
[06:21] Marcus: Operational ask — can the Redwood console expose per-route token cost during bursts so we can map cost to user journeys?
[06:29] Jordan: Yes, per-route cost breakdown is supported; we'll show the dashboard in the next demo.
[06:35] Samir: On timeline — we want to finish POC acceptance by mid-November if possible. is that realistic?
[06:41] Jordan: With one coordinated stress run and follow-ups, yes mid-November is doable. depends on test pass criteria.
[06:47] Evelyn: Acceptance criteria: p95 < 220ms for core payment flows under 1.5x baseline and no more than one fallback event in 24h during our simulated production window.
[06:58] Priya: Noted. we'll map those to the test plan.
[07:04] Jordan: Let's walk through immediate items before scheduling. Priya, you'll update runbook; Jordan will send sizing; Marcus will run the KV-heavy test; Lina will confirm KMS/audit details. correct?
[07:16] Marcus: correct.
[07:17] Lina: yes.
[07:19] Priya: yes, I'll also add the fallback threshold examples to the runbook and include the play links.
[07:26] Jordan: Great. Any other questions?
[07:28] Evelyn: One small question — we saw a mismatch in the agent label in logs last week, sometimes requests were attributed to Speaker 2 in the infra logs, leading to confusion. can that be normalized?
[07:38] Priya: That's likely a mapping issue in our telemetry ingestion; we'll fix the mapping and reprocess last week's traces on request.
[07:46] Samir: ok thanks.
[07:48] Jordan: Cool, we'll target the coordinated run Nov 10 and I'll send calendar invites after we confirm times.
[07:55] Evelyn: Sounds good. thanks everyone.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker attribution noise and brief audio dropouts between 00:36-01:05 and 05:10-05:30; some product names transcribed as 'Redwood Dedicat' in early notes.
